options.text: The ability to understand the internal state of a system by examining its outputs
The ability to deploy software faster
The number of unit tests in a system

questions.explanation: Observability is the ability to understand the internal state of a system by examining its outputs (telemetry: traces, metrics, logs).

questions.prompt: Distributed tracing is based on which three main signal types?
questions.explanation: Distributed tracing is based on three signals: logs, spans, and traces.

options.text: A single unit of work or operation, with name, timing, and attributes
The entire request path across all services

questions.explanation: A span represents a single unit of work/operation triggered by a request, containing a name, time-related data, log messages, and attributes.

questions.prompt: What is the first span of a trace called?
questions.explanation: A trace is made of one or more spans; the first one is the root span, representing the request from start to finish.

questions.prompt: Which metric instrument kind accumulates over time but can also go down again (e.g. queue length)?
questions.explanation: An UpDownCounter accumulates but can decrease (e.g. queue length); a Counter only goes up, a Gauge reads a current value, a Histogram aggregates client-side (e.g. latencies).

questions.prompt: Which statements about SLI and SLO are correct?

options.text: An SLI measures the behavior of the system, often capturing the user perspective
An SLO attaches business value to one or more SLIs
An SLI is a contract penalty clause
An SLO is a type of log format

questions.explanation: An SLI (Service Level Indicator) measures system behavior, often from the user perspective; an SLO (Service Level Objective) attaches business value to SLIs.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between sampling and tracing in profiling?

options.text: Sampling periodically interrupts the program with low overhead; tracing instruments calls with high detail but higher overhead
Sampling is more precise but slower than tracing
Tracing has lower overhead than sampling

questions.explanation: Sampling periodically interrupts and records the CPU state (low overhead, statistically accurate); tracing/instrumentation records function calls with high detail but higher overhead.

questions.prompt: In a flamegraph, the width of a function box represents how frequently that function was present in the collected samples.
questions.explanation: Flamegraph: the y-axis is stack depth, the x-axis spans the sample collection (alphabetical, not time), and box width is the frequency of that function in samples.

options.text: An open-source, vendor- and tool-agnostic observability framework for generating, exporting, and collecting telemetry

questions.explanation: OpenTelemetry is an open-source, vendor- and tool-agnostic observability framework for the generation, export, and collection of traces, metrics, and logs.
